after.PASSED and VALIDATED: proposed to the owner as a paper strategy of its own (rule 14) on the four index CFDs, a decision a month, sized by the risk engine, followed forward on paper; never real money. It is described as owning the market with an exit rule, not as an edge
after.otherwise: reported as it is; nothing changes

spec.data: Yahoo daily closes from 1927; month-end closes are each month's last close; each file's sha256 in the manifest
spec.dividends: not counted (price indices; ^GDAXI is a performance index)

gates.complete: every one of the 732 months 1929-01..1989-12 has its close and its decision
gates.costs_x2: mean net monthly return > 0 with the switching cost doubled
gates.smaller_crash: the worst peak-to-trough fall is smaller than holding the index all the time
gates.t: t of the mean net monthly return, 1929..1989, >= the threshold
gates.top_year: no calendar year supplies more than 50% of the total

spec.holdout_rule: the four index CFDs at equal weight, each with its own filter, over all 69 months 2021-01..2026-09: mean net monthly return > 0, > 0 with the cost doubled, and a worst fall smaller than holding all four all the time; a missing month fails it
spec.islamic: long or flat only; no short sale, no leverage, no interest-bearing instrument

periods.membership: a month belongs to the period of the month it is held

spec.question: does holding a stock index only while its month-end close is above its 10-month mean earn a positive net return, with a smaller worst fall than holding it all the time, in a swap-free account?
spec.rule: at each month-end close, hold the index for the next month if the close is above the mean of the last 10 month-end closes (this one included); otherwise hold nothing and earn nothing. A calendar month without a close is never bridged
